analyticalQuestion: On the sealed 15-case finite grid, does the gain remain bounded after normalization by the separately computed finite inviscid action proxy, do the registered a/b/c coefficients exhibit their expected epsilon hierarchy, and do the requested numerical discrepancy families remain below their frozen gates?
supportedTakeaway: Across five epsilon values and three finite cutoffs, the action-normalized gain lies between 0.9960745 and 0.9965851; at N=64 the registered b/epsilon and target-c/epsilon-squared ratios remain below 0.913 and 0.856, both cubic path alignments retain negative sign, and the largest gate-family ratio is below 0.116.
chartFamily: trend plus relationship plus signed comparison plus uncertainty-and-benchmark

dataSufficiency.fallback: Fail closed if any configured finite case, gate component, family maximum, independent result, or sealed-package binding is absent.
